findings.contrast: dose: CORR25 minus CORR15 and CORR35
findings.evidence: LPIPS full differences -0.05513 and +0.04727; preserved LPIPS -0.05607 and +0.04221; background SSIM +0.04160 and -0.03670; all respective Holm p <= 0.046875. CLIP target and directional CIs cross zero for both comparisons.
findings.interpretation: Increasing correction 15 to 35 improves source preservation by pixel and perceptual metrics; measured CLIP does not establish a corresponding change in target alignment. Dose is local coefficient, not equalized cross-arm realized correction impulse.

findings.evidence: preserved MAE -0.00562 CI [-0.01095,-0.00057], LPIPS preserved -0.01314 CI [-0.03062,-0.00025], SSIM +0.01194 CI [0.00449,0.01879]; Holm p 0.0781, 0.2344, 0.0938. CLIP image -0.00886 CI [-0.01724,-0.00128], Holm p 0.2832; DINO full -0.00212 CI crosses zero. CLIP target/directional CIs cross zero.
findings.interpretation: Pixel and LPIPS point estimates favor response routing for preservation, but adjusted evidence is inconclusive and CLIP image points in the opposite direction. This qualifies any pixel-only claim of consistent perceptual superiority. Same-state energy control does not imply exact matched realized cross-arm impulse.
Adding spatial memory gating to CORR25 worsens preservation by LPIPS in this comparison; evidence does not establish an editing benefit. Compare signed differences using CORR25 minus comparator.

CORR25 sacrifices text alignment on these proxies while source similarity differs by metric: full LPIPS favors CORR25, background SSIM favors FlowEdit. This directly qualifies a blanket preservation or editing superiority claim; compute differs.
RF shows substantially stronger source preservation on these metrics; directional CLIP point estimate favors CORR25 but adjusted evidence is inconclusive. RF has one seed per source.

mechanism_conclusion: Dose response supports a correction-strength/preservation association in this seen-source experiment; routing-specific superiority and editing success are not established by the available comparisons. Full-image metrics reflect source similarity across edited and preserved content, and target CLIP is only an alignment proxy. Existing earlier pixel-only claim text was not present in inspected R84 evidence, so comparisons address possible claims by metric rather than attributing an exact prior wording.
